summary: This Best Current Practice clarifies and updates requirements from RFCs 4787, 5382 and 5508 based on operational and development experience. It focuses on NAT from IPv4 to IPv4.

eli5.summary: Corrections to the rulebook for home-router address sharing, learned from real use.

subtitle: Clarifications and updates to the rules for IPv4 NAT behavior, drawn from operational experience.

tldr.problem: The NAT behavioral requirements in RFC 4787, RFC 5382 and RFC 5508 left several cases unspecified or unclear, such as how to track TCP sessions or what to do when an external address runs out of ports.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7857 goes through those gaps one by one and gives a clarification or an update for each, such as a TCP state machine for session tracking, protocol-dependent mapping and filtering by default, and rules for what refreshes a mapping.
tldr.outcome: It is a Best Current Practice that updates the three earlier RFCs and sets no requirements beyond them.

today: RFC 7857 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 4787, RFC 5382 and RFC 5508. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Scope and Purpose
sections.content:
RFC 4787 (UDP), RFC 5382 (TCP) and RFC 5508 (ICMP) set out how a NAT should behave. Operational experience from widespread deployment showed areas that needed clarification or updating, and RFC 7857 supplies them. It is published as BCP 127 and updates all three documents.

It focuses exclusively on NAT from IPv4 to IPv4 (NAT44) and says it does not create new requirements beyond those documents. Carrier-Grade NAT requirements are defined separately in RFC 6888. In this document, "NAT" covers both Basic NAT, which translates only IP addresses, and NAPT, which also translates transport identifiers such as ports or ICMP query IDs.
sections.eli5: The old rulebooks for sharing one address left some questions unanswered. This new note answers them.

sections.title: TCP Session Tracking and RST Handling
sections.content:
RFC 5382 defines TCP timers for connection states but not the state machine a NAT should follow when applying them. The update says that the simplified TCP state machine, adapted from RFC 6146, SHOULD be implemented for session tracking. Its states include CLOSED, INIT, ESTABLISHED, TRANS and the closing states that wait for both sides' FIN.

For the transitory idle-timeout, a NAT SHOULD offer separate configurable parameters for the open and closing timeouts. A default of at least 4 minutes is RECOMMENDED, although a NAT MAY allow a shorter configured value for deployments that find 4 minutes excessive for security.

For TCP RST, a NAT MUST translate an RST matching an existing mapping according to that mapping. It SHOULD then wait 4 minutes before deleting the session if no packets arrive. The RFC notes that the NAT has to verify that an RST belongs to a connection to avoid off-path attacks, and that removing the mapping immediately could leave stale connections if the first RST is lost.
sections.eli5: The router keeps a notebook of each conversation and waits a few minutes after a hang-up before it throws the page away, in case the hang-up message got lost.

sections.title: Mappings, Pooling and Filtering
sections.content:
Port overlapping. A NAT MAY reuse the same external port for connections from different internal address and port pairs, as long as their destinations differ. The NAT tracks the full 5-tuple (protocol, source address, source port, destination address, destination port). This helps when addresses are scarce.

Address pooling. With paired pooling (APP), new sessions from a host whose external address ran out of ports SHOULD be dropped. A configuration parameter MAY allow the NAT to use another external address instead, sometimes called soft-APP, at the cost of strict enforcement. The behavior SHOULD apply to TCP as well.

Protocol independence. Endpoint-independent mapping (EIM) SHOULD be protocol dependent, so an outbound TCP SYN does not create a mapping reused by UDP. Endpoint-independent filtering (EIF) SHOULD also be protocol dependent. Each can be made protocol independent with a configuration parameter, but the default MUST be protocol dependent.
sections.eli5: The router decides which outside number each inside device uses. The rules say it may share a number if the devices talk to different places, and that phone calls and letters keep separate lists by default.

sections.title: Mapping Refresh, Ports and Other Updates
sections.content:
Refresh. Even when inbound refresh is true, inbound packets that match an EIF mapping but do not create a new session due to a security policy SHOULD NOT refresh the mapping. Otherwise, a simple attack of one packet every two minutes could keep the mapping alive indefinitely. For outbound refresh, ICMP errors or TCP RST packets sent in response to inbound packets SHOULD NOT refresh the mapping.

Ports. A NAT MAY disable port parity preservation for all dynamic mappings, but SHOULD support means to explicitly request it, for example through the Port Control Protocol extension in RFC 7753. A NAT SHOULD follow Section 4 of RFC 6056 on port randomization.

Other items. The IP Identification field SHOULD be handled as in Section 5.3.1 of RFC 6864. ICMP Query mappings MAY be deleted once the last session using the mapping is deleted. For hairpinning of ICMP packets, the NAT must keep address mappings from external to internal addresses so that hairpinned ICMP Query sessions and ICMP errors work.
sections.eli5: A stranger who keeps knocking should not keep the door open forever. Likewise, the router picks outside numbers unpredictably so that nobody can easily guess them.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says some updates are inspired by NAT64, so the security considerations of RFC 6146 also apply. The port overlapping update allows more efficient use of NAT resources, but the NAT must not use it unless packets go to distinct destination addresses, to avoid service disruption.

The refresh updates and ICMP query mapping update prevent an illegitimate node from keeping mappings alive that should be cleared. Port randomization complicates tracking hosts behind a NAT. The IP ID update may hurt performance where fragmentation is massively experienced, and that could be used as an attack vector against NATs. Hosts that need restricted filtering are expected to enable policies such as an ACL locally or through a dedicated security device.
sections.eli5: Most of these fixes make the router harder to trick. One of them could slow the router down if a lot of broken-up packets arrive.
